restrictions: Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge (rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06, pad10*1), prefix rounds 0 through 5, all 256 output bits; every message is exactly 64 bytes (one block).

Generic birthday search over N = 2^128 messages in 2^96 groups of 2^32: group g has a fresh uniform 64-byte prefix P_g (two random 256-bit words) and message m(g,z) is P_g with LE32(z) XORed into bytes 0..3 and 40..43 (low halves of lanes 0 and 5, one theta column). Groups are processed in batches of 256 (one group per bit position of every 256-bit word, bitsliced), z = gray(t) for t = 0..2^32-1, slots offered in the fixed order decode_slot(q), q = 0..255.

Each z-step of a batch (256 messages) is an exact counted, fully unrolled word-RAM program (branches only in the ctz tree, the table step and the loop test) of at most 41,679 executed primitives on its worst path (all 32 Gray blocks cost the same): Gray update of the round-2 theta output A2 on 62 words with an exact incremental patch of the stored, theta'd round-3 input (chi difference of the 60 affected rows plus the induced D change), bitsliced rounds 3-5 in a fixed lane-complement encoding with theta added at the store, the digest-only last round fused with five delta-swap transpose stages, the remaining three stages, one Briggs-Torczon sparse-set step per message on the top 140 key bits (key of message n stored at address n), and loop control (ctz branch tree, no indirect jump). Rotations are address renamings, never executed. Charge: 41,679/256 + setup (< 2^-20) <= 162.81 operations = 162.81/1626 units per message.

Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers as our stated assumption (the program uses at most 56; table bases and constants are held in registers; a fixed-size register file whose operands are not memory accesses, 2 KiB, the size of a 32-entry 512-bit SIMD register file; the bound is not claimed under a memory-to-memory reading): one six-round permutation costs 1 unit; every executed load, store (direct or register-addressed), logic operation, shift, add, comparison, conditional branch, immediate move and random word costs 1/1626; constant addresses and immediates are instruction fields. Charging also one address addition per direct access and one move per ALU immediate gives 53,330 per z-step and 125.036; also each shift amount 55,634 and 125.097 (proof Section 9).

Time bound T <= 2^128*162.81/1626 + 3 < 2^124.67994 holds in every run (no restarts; the run halts at the first full-key match after at most 2 verification permutations). The success probability 0.39 (model value 0.39334) relies on the declared heuristic H1; output correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.

Credit: grouped partial evaluation, the sparse-set table, failure analysis and scaled-experiment design are due to jaazinn (0a5b7ae8, blake3-r2, in review), and the 256-message bit-plane Keccak and delta-swap transpose to may93182 (11c46f4d); both are credited as originators and named as co-authors in that sense. Lane-complement chi with folded round constants was brought to this track by tekkac (b001199a), after the Keccak team; the last-round early abort (only the 5 diagonal lanes feed the digest row) is ercumentyildirim's (c7fa1a56; r5: 4c969300); exact per-message charging follows zeeshan8281 (cbf7998d) and tekkac (f58275ef); the claimed reading matches the every-core-load-and-store-charged row of mitchuski's table (02d6a703). None has reviewed this package; the incremental round 2, theta at the store, the fused last round, table layout, counted program and any errors are ours.

No cryptanalytic weakness of SHA3 is claimed: this is a constant-factor improvement of a full-digest birthday search under the operation-level cost model. Memory is about 2^145 bytes (reported only, not a Pareto improvement).

heuristics.statement: For the failure events F1 and F2 (Section 7), the 2^128 keys of the grouped message set {m(g, z)} (independent uniform prefixes P_g, all z in {0,1}^32, processed in any fixed order chosen independently of the digests, in particular the order of Section 2: batch by batch, t = 0..2^32-1 with z = gray(t), slots p = decode_slot(q) = 64*floor(q/64) + 8*(q mod 8) + (floor(q/8) mod 8) for q = 0..255) behave like N independent uniform 256-bit values, i.e. Pr[F1] <= exp(-N(N-1)/2^257) and Pr[F2] <= N^3/6 * 2^-396.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability (Section 7) uses H1. Evaluator exactness, verification of every output, and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds are unconditional. Cross-group pairs (all but a 2^-96 fraction of pairs) provably collide with probability >= 2^-256 each (Cauchy-Schwarz over the uniform prefixes), so the expected number of colliding pairs is at least (1-2^-96)/2 without H1; H1 is needed for the second-moment behaviour behind Pr[F1] and for F2. Bitslicing, batching, the incremental round 2 and the fixed encodings change neither the message set nor any digest value (stored keys are digests XOR a fixed constant); they fix only the processing order, which depends on (batch, t, q) and never on digests.
heuristics.extrapolation: Tested at scale only: four organizer-executed scaled analogues with N_t = 2^9 messages and an 18-bit digest mask (N_t^2/2^18 = 1 = N^2/2^256), all computing digests with an evaluator that mirrors the counted program (incremental round 2, lane-complement rounds with theta at the store, fused last round, transpose stage order, processing order): 256 groups x 2 (a full batch), 16 groups x 32, a single group of 512 (strongest within-group structure) and 4 groups x 128 with the varying z bits at 25..31. Every organizer trial checks full 256-bit keys against an independent direct sponge (its first 4 and one at every step t = 2^i), the 62-word support of each Gray coefficient column, and the incrementally maintained round-3 input against a rebuild. Local runs (all reported, proof Section 10.3): an organizer-runner replay at 256 trials per layout (100/109/107/111), a 256-trial timing run, two batches of 8,192 trials per layout (pooled z +0.9/+1.2/+1.3/-1.1, one cell of eight at +2.2), and ten further organizer-runner replays on fresh seeds during internal review (totals 1,004/980/994/958 of 2,560, z -0.1/-1.1/-0.5/-2.0; lowest cell 75 of 256 at -3.3 sd, spread layout, seed rv-coin-f). Pooled over all runs (19,456 trials per layout) the z-scores are +0.9/+0.9/+1.2/-1.6 (full-width/spread/single-group/high-z). The claim extrapolates uniform-model behaviour to N = 2^128 and the full 256-bit key.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is not proved. Within a group the round-2 theta output A2 is exactly affine in z (Lemma 2), a stronger structure than in a generic search; five further nonlinear chi layers (rounds 2-6) follow, but masked low-width experiments cannot exclude a structural effect that appears only at full width. Within a group the digest has degree at most 2^5 = 32 in z; z has 32 bits, so no degree-based zero-sum exists on any affine subspace of z (that needs dimension at least 33). The experiments use a full dictionary of masked keys, so the top-140-bit loss F2 is bounded only under H1. Organizer seeds are public. The scaled experiments resolve the success frequency only to about +-0.03 at 256 trials. The 0.0033 allowance between the model value 0.39334 and the claimed 0.39 is not statistically certified.
